_about: Things a person (or a later check) found that the checks of the day missed, each turned into a general rule and a system change that now catches it. Successor of docs/quality-failure-corpus.json (the old critic system's corpus, 7 incidents), kept to its rules: the generalized failure and the invariant name nothing from one game (tools/kitcheck.mjs checks against the manifest's nouns); prevention is never 'remind the reviewer' alone; every entry names the check (tools/checks.json) that now catches it, or says it is still open. Add an entry whenever Desmic or a player finds something the checks passed. See docs/QUALITY-SYSTEM.md.

escapes.symptom: The game looked soft on the phone: adaptive resolution had fallen to about 0.6x on every quality tier to hold 45 fps.
escapes.why_missed: The checks measured frame rate only, never the resolution it was bought with; headless runs can't show a phone's sharpness.
escapes.generalized_failure: Frame-rate adaptation trades away sharpness without a floor, and no measurement reports the resolution a device actually renders at.
escapes.invariant: Every quality tier has a resolution floor; the frame-rate test reports resolution alongside frame rate, swept over several resolutions, and devices are compared in megapixels.

prevention.what: quality tiers carry minPixelRatio (Medium 0.8, chosen by Desmic 4 Oct)
kit/bench.ts resolution sweep (0.6 to 2x), wake lock, in-app web view noted
frame-rate verdicts are recorded per build (tools/verdict.mjs --lane performance)

escapes.symptom: Why to play and how to play were both unclear; the abduction didn't read; cards at the bottom pulled the eye away from the world; some lines spoon-fed.
escapes.why_missed: The checks proved the game could be finished; nothing measured what a newcomer understood, and the AI play-testers of the day were briefed with the design.
escapes.generalized_failure: Checks prove a game can be finished, while nothing measures, cold, whether a newcomer understands why to play, how to play and what is being taught.
escapes.invariant: A cold account (place, who, goal, controls, lesson) is recorded before the design is read, then compared with the intent generated from the game's own data; each gap is a finding in the comprehension lane.

prevention.what: tools/playserver.mjs refuses /intent until the cold account and the first-look verdict are in; gaps become results
tools/intent.mjs generates the intent from manifest, beats, stations and learning designs
speech and prompts live in the world (kit/overlay.ts), never a bottom card for a speaker with a body

escapes.status: partial: an AI player approximates a newcomer; a real beginner play-test is still owed

escapes.symptom: On a phone: a skipped cold-open line stayed under the real one; the thumb-stick hint sat far from the stick; townsfolk bubbles escaped the overlay so prompts landed on their text; stale thoughts appeared long after their moment.
escapes.why_missed: Every scripted check clicked with a mouse on one screen shape.
escapes.generalized_failure: Automated play used one input mode and one screen shape, so input- and layout-specific defects were invisible.
escapes.invariant: Every input mode the game supports is played start to end on its own screen shape, through the controls a player of that device uses, with a contact sheet a person can scan.

prevention.what: playthrough runs flowcheck as touch (393x760, taps, stick) and keyboard (1024x640, E/Space/1-2/WASD)
manifest.input lists the modes; html[data-input] says which the game believes
everything pinned in the world goes through one overlay host with declutter

escapes.symptom: Standing where two words were close, the prompt named the nearer one, not the one the player was looking at; one word was hard to pick at all.
escapes.why_missed: The scripted run posed the player beside each target, where nearest and aimed agree.
escapes.generalized_failure: Targeting picked the nearest candidate, so the prompt could name something other than what the player was looking at.
escapes.invariant: The action prompt names what the player aims at (the smallest angle within a cone of the look direction), falling back to the nearest; tests approach targets with the camera aimed, not only posed beside them.

prevention.what: kit/target.ts pickTarget: aimed (within ~35 degrees) beats near, lined-up things defer to priority; used by the words and by the island's things and notes. Between a word and the engine, words still come first (an aim contest hid a word from the 4 Oct newcomer)
flowcheck aims the camera at words; speedrun reports places where one prompt hides another

escapes.symptom: Editing the save in the browser resumed at the last stop with none of the learning done.
escapes.why_missed: No check edited saves; progress was a plain checkpoint name.
escapes.generalized_failure: Progress was stored as a position, so a hand-edited or copied save could skip the learning it stands for.
escapes.invariant: A checkpoint is only resumed when the learning record shows the stations it requires; otherwise the game resumes at the furthest checkpoint the record supports. Forged records remain a known client-side limit until progress is signed on a server.

prevention.what: kit/progress.ts + kit/save.ts: loadVerified
manifest.progress: order, requires, names
breaker tamper cases generated from the progress spec; speedrun checks each checkpoint was earned

escapes.status: partial: forged learning records are still believed (warned)

found.where: Galaxy F15, frame-rate test inside the Claude app

escapes.symptom: The phone went to sleep while the benchmark ran.
escapes.why_missed: The benchmark was only ever run on machines that don't sleep.
escapes.generalized_failure: A measurement that runs without input for minutes didn't keep the device awake.
escapes.invariant: Long measurements on a device hold a wake lock (or a muted-video fallback) and report the environment they ran in (browser or in-app web view).

prevention.what: kit/bench.ts keepAwake() and environment line

found.by: Claude, after the harness started warning about unwalkable test spots
found.where: break tester, phone mode, mash segment

escapes.symptom: The 'mash the notes' probe passed with 0 notes in the satchel and 0 Gate answers: its taps had timed out on prompts still popping in, so nothing it claimed to test had happened.
escapes.why_missed: The probe only checked that nothing bad happened afterwards; with its setup silently skipped, that is always true.
escapes.generalized_failure: A probe whose setup silently failed still passed, because it only checked that nothing bad happened afterwards.
escapes.invariant: Every probe checks that its setup happened; if it did not, the result is unresolved (the gate shows it), never a pass. Test spots are checked to be places a player can stand.

prevention.what: breaker reports 'unresolved' when the mash setup isn't reached; a thumb waits for a popping-in prompt to hold still
harness pose warns on any spot the game's walkable probe rejects, on every island

found.by: Desmic, leaving the game on screen on his PC; measured by Claude with a frame-by-frame pose log and frame bursts on his GPU
found.where: every idle character: the player and the townsfolk

escapes.symptom: Characters flickered while standing idle: about once a second a body part snapped to its rest pose for one frame (14-48 degrees) and back.
escapes.why_missed: The cloud harness renders at a few frames a second, so a one-frame pop falls between captured frames; nothing compared a character's pose from one frame to the next; testers move, and the pop only shows while standing still.
escapes.generalized_failure: A rig reset its bones to rest before the animation mixer ran, but the mixer skips writing a bone whose value did not change since its last write, so whenever a clip held still the bone was left at rest for a frame.
escapes.invariant: Layered motion starts each frame from the pose the mixer last left, never from rest; standing idle, no bone moves more than a few degrees between frames.

prevention.what: kit/pose-hold.ts: restore the mixer's last pose before mixer.update, keep it right after, then layer motion on; used by both rigs
kittest plays the real idle clip through a mixer both ways: resetting to rest pops (the bug reproduced), holding the last pose never moves a bone more than 3 degrees a frame
&flicklog=1 logs pose jumps, resolution steps, fades, shader compiles and hitches; tools/desktop/flicktest.cmd runs it on a real GPU with frame bursts

found.where: the town's west rail, behind the planters

escapes.symptom: Two standing townsfolk filled the one gap of a walkway, turning it into a dead end; the player only got out with "Return to arrival".
escapes.why_missed: The narrow-strip scan saw two short pieces either side of the townsfolk (each under its length limit), and nothing compared walking with and without the people standing about.
escapes.generalized_failure: Characters placed as solid obstacles can close a way through, or cut a narrow passage into short pieces that pass a strip check, without any map check noticing.
escapes.invariant: With every character standing where it stands, the walk between the two sides of each one is no more than a few metres longer than with nobody about, and no part of the map is cut off.

prevention.what: reachprobe floods the walkable grid with and without the townsfolk: nothing cut off, and no townsperson lengthens the way past them by more than 4 m (proven to fail on the old placement)
the chatting pair moved onto the open terrace; the rail strip and the dead-end alley behind the planters closed
